identification: Old full-size looking violin in a black coffin-style case with red velvet lining, two bows, Hidersine rosin and a packet of Wing steel strings. Dark red-brown varnish, heavily worn on the top and lower bout, strings slack, tailpiece and fittings look ordinary. Back and label not visible. Looks like a typical early-to-mid 20th century German or Czech trade violin (Strad copy type). Nothing in the photo points to a named maker.

viewing_check: Look through the f-hole and photograph the internal label (maker, town, date, Stradivarius copy text, Made in Czechoslovakia/Germany). Photograph the back (one-piece or two-piece, flame, cracks), check for open seams, top cracks or sound post patches, and the neck/scroll. Check the bows for stamps on the frog or stick and whether hair, tips and heads are intact; a stamped or silver-mounted bow can be worth more than the violin.
